_comment: FunctionDeploymentRequest body for the function registered by
horizon-shield-function.json. Validated by gate G10 against the
FunctionDeploymentRequest / GpuSpecificationDto schemas in the vendored
OpenAPI document.
The choices that are not arbitrary:
minInstances 1        - scale-to-zero is right for inference and wrong
for a safety plane. A cold start is a window in
which agents can be invoked and the Shield
cannot. The invariant chain is CPU work, so a
held replica costs almost nothing.
maxRequestConcurrency - 16, bounded well under TransactionCycle's
max_members (32), so the epoch buffer is what
refuses excess load, not the HTTP layer, and it
refuses with a 429 that means what NVCF says it
means: the request did not run, retry later.
maxInstances 1        - the decision plane is a SERIALISATION POINT.
Two replicas would each open their own epoch, and
two agents whose actions conflict could land in
different epochs and both be admitted -- the
exact failure the transaction exists to remove.
Horizontal scaling here is not a tuning knob; it
is a correctness bug. Scale the AGENTS, not this.
gpu/instanceType      - required by the schema. Horizon's chain is CPU
work; the smallest GPU instance is selected
because NVCF's placement is GPU-indexed, not
because a GPU is used.
